stances_toward.note: The IMF is the constraint Nairobi cooperates with out of necessity and resists in practice. The USD 3.6bn programme ended in April 2025 before its last review (sources differ on whether both sides agreed to drop it), a year after the street defeated the Finance Bill 2024; staff missions in September-October 2025 and 24 February - 4 March 2026 talked about a new programme, the Eurobond prospectus of February 2026 called the talks an effort to align any programme with Kenya's 'fiscal and economic priorities', the Finance Minister said the budget does not count on IMF money, and a new mission was being prepared in August 2026. Securitisation of revenue streams initially complicated the talks (Reuters). Reluctant partner: the Fund is wanted as a seal for markets, not as a policy; a source calling the relationship 'reluctant' was not found, so the grade is our reading (B because two independent reports agree on the facts). Bond none.

stances_toward.note: The IMF is Lebanon's route back to credit: the 2022 staff-level agreement stalled for lack of reforms; in August 2026 parliament passed the bank resolution law, which the IMF welcomed as a significant step (the president referred one amendment on central-bank independence to the Constitutional Council); Georgieva met Salam on 29 September. A new staff-level agreement still needs the financial gap law, a 2027 budget and a medium-term fiscal framework (and, per the mid-September mission, a VAT rise to 12%). Partner, warming - but conditioned; the government is moving faster than any since 2019. Bond none.
